tasks.old_behavior: When an unrecognized subcommand is given, the error message displays: usage: git-gui [{blame|browser|citool}]
tasks.new_behavior: When an unrecognized subcommand is given, the error message now displays: usage: git-gui [{blame|browser|citool|gui|pick}]
tasks.compatibility_reason: The user-visible error/usage message format has changed. Any wrapper script, integration test, or documentation that parses or matches the exact usage string will see a different output. While the semantic behavior (exit code 1, error output) is preserved, the exact text has changed.
tasks.test_recommendation: Invoke git-gui with an invalid subcommand (e.g., 'git gui bogus') and verify that (a) the usage message contains the new subcommand list, (b) exit code remains 1, and (c) the error is still delivered via the same channel (stderr on non-Win32, tk_messageBox on Win32).

strategy.preferred_artifact: single command line or regression test in the project's CLI test framework
strategy.trigger_surface: run the command/option combination that exercises the changed behavior
strategy.required_observation: byte-level stdout/stderr or parsed structured-output schema

required_output.goal: produce one command or code artifact that reaches target_location.new_lines
must_include: exact command(s) or generated code path
expected reachability signal such as return code, log, output, coverage, breakpoint, or tracepoint
input values that exercise old/new compatibility behavior
contract_probe with before/after commands and the registered comparison oracle
required_output.do_not_execute: Generate artifacts and commands; do not run destructive or privileged tests unless the user explicitly asks.
